_about: PLACEHOLDER story beats. Replace with the writer's story (see docs/STORY_TEMPLATE.md). One section per night.

1.open: Mission Control: Mabuhay, Commander! Welcome to Bulalakaw Station. Tonight, learn the battery and keep an eye on the cameras.
1.close: Mission Control: You found the leak like a real engineer. Salamat, see you tomorrow!

malfunction.title: WHY IS POWER LEAKING?

clues.text: Sparks near the panel plug!
The heater dial says MID, like it should.

malfunction.why: Loose connections turn electricity into heat and sparks instead of useful power.

radio: A day on Mars is called a sol. It lasts 24 hours and 39 minutes.
Sunlight on Mars is less than half as strong as on Earth.
Rovers plan every sol around how much energy they have.

2.open: Mission Control: Maya has joined you. Tonight: fresh air and food! New: tap ASK to send us a question. Light takes minutes to get here, so ask early!
2.close: Mission Control: Good air, good food, happy crew. Ingat!

malfunction.title: WHY IS THE AIR GETTING STALE?

clues.text: The CO2 gauge near the filter reads high.
Airlock pressure gauge: steady.
Maya: the plants look green and healthy!

malfunction.why: A clogged filter can't pull carbon dioxide out of the air, so the air gets stale.

radio: Mars air is about 95% carbon dioxide.
NASA's MOXIE made oxygen from Mars air: 122 grams in total.
Plants need light, water and warmth.

3.open: Mission Control: Mateo is here. A small particle storm is coming: practise sheltering!
3.close: Mission Control: Light first, particles later. You beat them!

malfunction.title: WHY DID THE SHELTER ALARM BEEP?

clues.text: A thin line of light shows around the door.
Sensor self-test: PASSED.
Door battery meter: FULL.

malfunction.why: Even a thin crack lets particles through: shielding only works with no gaps.

radio: Radiation is invisible, so we measure it with dosimeters.
In September 2017, Curiosity measured radiation 2 to 3 times higher than normal.
Water and plastic are good shielding because they contain lots of hydrogen.

4.open: Mission Control: Carlo is on an EVA tonight. Talk to Earth: messages take minutes!
4.close: Mission Control: Message received, Commander. Eleven minutes later!

malfunction.title: WHY ARE EARTH MESSAGES SLOW?

clues.text: Earth's signal shows up off to one side.
A dust devil passed by the dish!
Radio box power meter: normal.
Carlo: the dish looks clean to me.

malfunction.why: A dish must point straight at Earth. Even a small turn makes the signal much weaker.

radio: Radio signals take 3 to 22 minutes to travel between Mars and Earth.
NASA's Deep Space Network listens from California, Spain and Australia.
When Perseverance landed in 2021, its signal took 11 minutes 22 seconds.

5.open: Mission Control: A huge dust storm, like the real one in 2018. Keep everything running!
5.close: Mission Control: The storm couldn't stop you. Kaya natin 'to!

malfunction.title: WHY IS THE BASE USING EXTRA POWER?

clues.text: The fan sounds rough and slow.
Lamp current: normal.
Battery cell temperatures look a bit warm.
Grey dust on the fan blades!

malfunction.why: Dust makes fans work harder, and a harder-working fan uses more power.

radio: In 2018 a dust storm covered all of Mars.
Dust devils sometimes cleaned rover solar panels!
The Opportunity rover worked for more than 5,000 sols.

6.open: Mission Control: Tonight replays the real X12 solar flare of May 20, 2024. Be ready!
6.close: Mission Control: Light is faster than particles, and so were you!

malfunction.title: WHY IS THE SKY RADAR GLITCHING?

clues.text: A cable by the airlock wall is hanging loose.
Radar box temperature: cool.
The radar dish looks dusty.
Lani: I can see sparks on the radar cable!

malfunction.why: A loose cable makes signals flicker on and off, so the screen glitches.

radio: This is a real event: an X12 flare hit Mars on May 20, 2024.
Curiosity measured 8,100 microgray that day, about 30 chest X-rays.
NASA's MAVEN saw auroras glow over Mars during that storm.

7.open: Mission Control: The finale! Dust, a flare and a blackout. Send your discovery before the link goes dark!
7.close: Mission Control: Discovery received! The supply ship is coming in. Mabuhay, Bulalakaw Station!

malfunction.title: WHY IS THE GREENHOUSE LOSING WATER?

clues.text: A puddle under the pipes!
Airlock vent: closed and locked.
The recycler light blinks yellow.
Maya: I hear dripping behind the plants.

malfunction.why: On Mars every drop counts: the space station recycles about 98% of its water.

radio: Tonight combines two real events: the 2018 dust storm and the 2024 flare.
Space rocks hit Mars more often than Earth because its air is so thin.
Send it now: a message takes minutes to reach Earth!
